name: Marleth Barleybrew
summary: Marleth Barleybrew is an ambitious dwarven brewer stationed out in Brewnall Village. Frustrated by the Thunderbrew clan's dominance over the local beer market, she constantly schemes to prove her family's brew is superior to Kharanos's famous Thunder Ale.

sections.title: The Brewing Rivalry
sections.body: In Dun Morogh, alcohol is taken as seriously as steel, and the rivalry between the Barleybrew and Thunderbrew families is legendary. Marleth Barleybrew resents the near-monopoly that Ragnar Thunderbrew and his kin maintain out of the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Convinced her own craft is every bit as robust, she seeks clever ways to slip Barleybrew kegs into the hands of tavern patrons. Rather than engaging in open conflict, she opts for petty subterfuge, recruiting passing travelers to secretly swap out Kharanos's prized ale casks with her own.

faq.answer: Marleth is a dwarf brewmaster residing in Brewnall Village in western Dun Morogh. She represents the Barleybrew family and actively works to challenge the rival Thunderbrew family's stranglehold on the local drinking scene.

faq.q: Where can I find Marleth Barleybrew?
faq.answer: She can be found in Brewnall Village, located in the western reaches of Dun Morogh near Iceflow Lake.

faq.q: Why does Marleth want to swap Thunderbrew's beer?
faq.answer: Marleth believes her family's ale is just as good as, if not better than, Thunder Ale. Because the Thunderbrews dominate the trade in Kharanos, she hires adventurers to covertly replace the tavern's kegs with Barleybrew stock so drinkers will taste her product, while bringing back a sample of Thunder Ale for her to analyze.

faq.q: Who are the other members of the Barleybrew family?
faq.answer: Her extended clan includes other noted brewers and tradesmen such as Malgin, Rejold, Wellart, and Yorus Barleybrew, all dedicated to the craft of traditional dwarven brewing.

angles.text: For dwarves, brewing is an art form tied intimately to clan prestige, making Marleth's feud with the Thunderbrews a matter of fierce family pride.
